Neil Miller was transported to Maple Heights Jail and booked on counts of abduction, kidnapping, failure to comply with an officer and obstructing official business. Officers discovered that Neil had a warrant for his arrest out of neighboring Summit County for failing to report for probation, stemming from a 2023 conviction of attempted theft, aggravated theft, and identity fraud. Officers were also able to establish that the Dodge Durango that Neil was driving belonged to his mother and was not stolen. However, a subsequent search of the vehicle uncovered, nine different cell phones as well as an Apple laptop, which appeared to belong to an unknown third party. These items were confiscated and officers attempted to return them. However, they were unable to locate any owners, so no charges were brought. Neil entered a not guilty plea for all charges, and a judge set his bond at $5,000. Two weeks later, bond was changed to $25,000 which Neil posted. In May 2024, Neil changed his plea, presumably after entering a plea deal, where the charges of kidnapping and obstructing official business were dropped in exchange for pleading guilty to abduction and failure to comply with an officer. He was sentenced to 18 months in prison and ordered to serve a minimum of one year of post-release control. While incarcerated, Summit County filed charges against Neil and convicted him for theft an aggravated possession of drugs. He was given a six-month sentence to run concurrently with his prison sentence. Neil was released from prison in October 2025 and is currently serving his one-year period of post-release supervision.
